CHARTER-OFFERING DEVIATION REPORT: Atherton Biomedical, Inc. IPO
Documents: Fourth A&R Certificate of Incorporation filed 6/22/2023 ("Charter"); Underwriting Agreement dated 1/6/2025 ("UA"); Preliminary Prospectus dated 1/3/2025 ("Prelim"). Prelim and UA describe a future "IPO Charter" that is not in the file; Charter is the only charter text supplied.

BOTTOM LINE
Three groups of problems. (1) Charter is internally defective on authorized preferred (CRITICAL). (2) The Charter conflicts with the IPO Charter that UA 6(j) and Prelim describe on nine governance points; this is expected only if the IPO Charter is actually filed, but UA Exhibit A attaches the 4th A&R itself, not an IPO Charter, so no draft embodies 6(j) or Prelim. (3) UA and Prelim conflict on greenshoe, share count, lock-up, effectiveness, settlement and fees. Items are rated Critical (C), High (H), Medium (M), Low (L). Unverified legal points are marked (eCFR fetch blocked).

A. CHARTER VS. IPO CHARTER (UA 6(j)) AND PRELIM
1. Authorized preferred exceeds authority (C). Charter 4.1(b) authorizes 25,000,000 preferred; 4.4(a), 4.5(a), 4.6(a) designate 8,200,000 + 11,650,000 + 6,800,000 = 26,650,000 (1,650,000 over). UA 3(b) repeats 25,000,000 authorized and represents all preferred "duly authorized and validly issued"; Prelim Capitalization treats 26,650,000 as outstanding. Over-issuance risks void/voidable stock (DGCL 151, 161, 204/205 ratification, unverified) and undermines the UA 3(b) rep, the Qualified IPO conversion and Hargrove Whitfield's 6(e) opinion. Action: obtain stock ledger/prior charters (2018, 2020, 2021 restatements are not supplied), determine actual issued shares, and ratify under DGCL 204/205 before the IPO Charter is filed.
2. Board structure (H). Charter 5.3: every director elected annually (no classes). UA 6(j)(iii) and Prelim (Risk Factors; Classified Board) require three staggered classes. Prelim also lists seven directors (Nagarajan, Marchetti, Durand-Phelps, Okonkwo, Rajagopal, Belasco, Fong) with Class I/II/III terms but assigns no class; UA says assignment is "in the IPO Charter" (not supplied). Charter 5.5 and 4.4(i)/4.5(i)/4.6(i) preferred director seats (Series A, B (voting with A), C) must be extinguished;
3. Director removal (H). Charter silent (DGCL default: without cause by majority). UA 6(j)(iv)/Prelim: for cause only, 66 2/3%.
4. Written consent (H). Charter 6.3 permits stockholder written consent. UA 6(j)(vi)/Prelim prohibit it post-closing.
5. Cumulative voting (L). Charter silent; UA 6(j)(v)/Prelim require express denial.
6. Section 203 (H). Charter Art. IX opts out; UA 6(j)(ix) forbids any opt-out; Prelim says 203 applies. Charter must be amended; Prelim statement is accurate only post-filing.
7. Forum (H). Charter 8.1 has no Securities Act federal-forum clause (so Prelim "will provide" is unsupported by the existing Charter), and its fallback is Delaware Superior Court then D. Del. UA 6(j)(vii)(A) fallback is "another state court in Delaware" then D. Del.; Prelim says Chancery then federal court in Delaware (omits state-court tier). Three different cascades. Federal forum clause validity: Salzberg v. Sciabacucchi (Del. 2020) (from memory, unverified). Charter 8.1(b) covers "employee, or agent"; UA/Prelim omit "agent". Prelim excludes Exchange Act claims; UA is silent.
8. Amendments (H). Charter Art. X: majority vote. UA 6(j)(viii)/Prelim: 66 2/3% for classified board, removal, written consent and forum. UA also covers adopting inconsistent provisions; Prelim does not.
9. Capital (M). Charter: 100,000,000 common/25,000,000 preferred. UA 6(j)(i): "not fewer than" 200,000,000 / 10,000,000 blank-check; Prelim states exactly 200,000,000/10,000,000.
10. Elimination of preferred (H). UA 6(j)(ii) refers to eliminating "certificates of designation"; the Charter creates Series A-C in the charter itself (Art. IV), not by certificates of designation; wording mismatch. UA 6(j)(x) also eliminates "preemptive rights, rights of first refusal, co-sale rights": Charter 4.2.4 already denies preemptive rights; ROFR/co-sale are contractual (investor agreements not supplied) and not charter items; Prelim says registration rights survive (Registration Rights, Shares Eligible), consistent with UA lock-up Exhibit C(c) but UA 6(j)(x) bars "other preferential rights" - confirm registration rights are outside the charter.
11. Conversion mechanics and sequencing (H). Charter 4.4(d)/4.5(d)/4.6(d): auto-conversion on "closing" of Qualified IPO ($50,000,000 gross proceeds to Company and at least $10.00/share). Pricing range $18-$20 and 8,500,000 x $19 = $161,500,000 satisfy it, but only at closing (Jan. 17). UA 6(j) requires the IPO Charter be filed "at or prior to" closing stating no preferred outstanding, and UA 4(e) requires selling stockholders' preferred be converted "prior to the Closing Date" (needed to deliver common at closing). Circularity: series cannot be eliminated before conversion that is triggered by closing. Action: written elections/consents under 4.4(d)(ii) (A majority), 4.5(d)(ii) (B majority), 4.6(d)(ii) (C 60%) to convert before pricing, conditioned on closing; Prelim ("immediately prior to completion") should be conformed.
12. Votes needed for the IPO Charter (H). Charter 4.4(f)/(g), 4.5(f)/(g): A and B majorities; 4.6(f)/(g): Series C 60% separate vote. Eliminating series rights is an adverse change needing those votes plus Art. X majority. UA 3(c) says approvals "have been or will be taken"; no evidence. Series C holders have full ratchet (4.6(e)), 3x capped participation (4.6(b)), and a redemption right (4.6(h), 5th anniversary of unstated issue date): obtain waivers.
13. Series C debt covenant (H). Charter 4.6(g)(v) requires 60% Series C consent for debt over $10,000,000. Prelim shows debt $41,300,000 (Capitalization/Summary Financial Data). No disclosure that consent was obtained; UA 3(f) compliance rep exposure. Confirm consent.
14. Charter internal inconsistencies (M). 4.4(c) Series A dividends "prior and in preference" while 4.5(c)/4.6(c) say pari passu with A; 4.4(g)(iii) protects A against senior or pari passu series only; 4.7(c) treats plain liquidation as a Deemed Liquidation Event (circular); A and B participation uncapped vs C capped at 3x; 4.4(g)(vi) cross-refers "Section 4.7". Series C 5th anniversary date undefined in the file.
15. Charter execution (L). Signature block (Diane Kowalski) is blank in the file copy; obtain certified filed copy. File No. 6347821, 3/14/2017 incorporation and registered agent match UA/Prelim.
16. Prelim omits (M): special meetings (Charter 6.2), board-only vacancies (5.4), exculpation (7.1) and indemnification/advancement (7.2).

B. UNDERWRITING AGREEMENT VS. PRELIMINARY PROSPECTUS
17. Over-allotment (C). UA 1/2(b): 1,725,000 Option Shares (15% of 11,500,000); Prelim cover, Use of Proceeds, Underwriting and Capitalization n.4: 1,500,000. Prelim full-exercise table ($247,000,000 public; $177,650,000 to Company) uses 1,500,000; at 1,725,000 Company proceeds before expenses would be 10,225,000 x $17.765 = $181,644,625 (not $177,650,000). Also option is company-only in both; Schedule I says no selling-stockholder option shares.
18. Share count/capitalization (C). UA 3(b): 42,350,000 "outstanding" = 12,500,000 founders + 26,650,000 converted preferred + 3,200,000 option/RSU shares. Prelim: 42,350,000 = 15,700,000 common + 26,650,000, yet also "excludes" 3,200,000 option/RSU shares. 12,500,000 + 3,200,000 = 15,700,000, so Prelim's actual common includes unissued option shares and then excludes them again (or UA overstates). If options are not outstanding, true outstanding is 39,150,000 and post-offering 47,650,000, not 50,850,000. This flows into Prelim's 39,350,000 restricted shares, NTBV per share ($3.50, $5.88), dilution ($13.12), 5,080,000 plan reserve "approximately 10%" and ownership table.
19. Effectiveness (C). UA 3(d) represents the Registration Statement "has been declared effective" and Rule 430A complied with, on 1/6/2025; Prelim (1/3/2025) is "subject to completion", price blank, cover says securities may not be sold until effective; UA 6(a) makes effectiveness a condition. UA is dated before pricing (1/14) with price blank. Also 3(k)/6(h): Nasdaq "has been approved" vs Prelim "have applied".
20. Settlement (H). UA 1 and 2(c): T+3 (pricing 1/14, closing 1/17). Current Exchange Act Rule 15c6-1 standard is T+1 (since 5/28/2024), with T+2 for firm-commitment offerings priced after 4:30 p.m. ET and parties' express agreement under (d) (unverified; fetch blocked). Confirm compliance or shorten.
21. Lock-up scope and term (H). Prelim: 180 days from "date of this prospectus"; cover says Company, directors/officers and selling stockholders; body says holders of "substantially all". UA 6(i): directors, officers and holders of 1% or more; Exhibit C: 180 days after the date of the UA (1/6), while UA 1/5(i)/6(i) say final Prospectus. Exhibit C exceptions (gifts with donee lock-up, family/trusts, entity distributions, DROs, 10b5-1 plan, option exercise/RSU, tax withholding) differ from Prelim's (nominee/custodian, will/intestacy, affiliates). Exhibit C(c) bars registration demands; Prelim says demand/piggyback rights exist and does not mention suspension. Company lock-up: UA 5(i) exceptions (Company/Option Shares, existing awards, plan grants with lock-ups) do not carve out the Form S-8 Prelim says will be filed "promptly after the completion" (Equity Incentive Plan). Sub-1% holders are unlocked under UA, contra Prelim.
22. Indemnification (M). Prelim: "we and the selling stockholders will indemnify" generally; UA 7(b): Selling Stockholders liable only for information they furnished, several not joint, capped at net proceeds.
23. Expenses (M). Prelim: Company "reimburse[s] the underwriters for certain expenses"; UA 9: Underwriters pay Calloway Reeves & Thornton; Company reimburses (cap $300,000) only if the offering fails due to Company's breach. Prelim expense amount blank; FINRA treatment of reimbursement (unverified).
24. Underwriter default (M). Prelim says non-defaulting commitments may be increased or the UA terminated on default; UA 2(c) has several obligations only and no default-substitution clause. UA 8 termination events (market suspension, banking moratorium, hostilities, MAE, failed condition) are not described in Prelim, which cites only MAC and deliverables.
25. Selling stockholders undisclosed (H). Prelim cover says selling stockholders are "identified in this prospectus" but no table appears. UA Schedule I: Redhill Ventures Fund III, L.P. 1,500,000 (signatory Gregory Okonkwo); Solstice Health Capital Partners, L.P. 1,200,000 (Sunita Rajagopal); Dr. Julian Marchetti 300,000. Total 3,000,000 ties. Okonkwo and Rajagopal are directors (Prelim list; UA 6(i)), a related-party/independence point; Prelim cross-refers to "Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions" which is absent. UA 3(o) no-undisclosed-relationships rep is thereby at risk.
26. Power of attorney (M). UA Exhibit D appoints Diane Kowalski, Company General Counsel, as attorney-in-fact for selling stockholders; conflict with Company interests (and with Marchetti, a Company officer). Also Kowalski signs notices for the Company.

C. FINANCIAL AND ARITHMETIC ERRORS IN PRELIM
29. Net proceeds (H). Use of Proceeds says $151.0 million "after deducting underwriting discount and estimated offering expenses"; the figure $151,002,500 equals 8,500,000 x $17.765, i.e., before expenses (UA 2(a) and Underwriting table say "before expenses"). Cash pro forma as adjusted $215,702,500 = $64,700,000 + $151,002,500, ignoring expenses (amount blank).
30. Equity inconsistency (H). Pro forma stockholders' equity $109,426,000 and as-adjusted $260,386,150, but NTBV pro forma is $148.2 million and as-adjusted $299.2 million; NTBV cannot exceed equity absent negative intangibles/disclosed adjustments. As-adjusted APIC $371,185,300 does not equal $220,233,650 + $151,002,500 - $8,500 par ($371,227,650), a $42,350 difference. Historical NTBV $(22.4) million / 15,700,000 = $(1.43) ties.
31. Dilution table (H). Shows new investors buying 8,500,000 shares and existing holders retaining 42,350,000 (83.3%/16.7%); but 11,500,000 shares are sold to new investors and selling stockholders hold 39,350,000 afterward. Existing consideration $148,225,000 (= 42,350,000 x $3.50) uses NTBV, not consideration paid. Total $309,725,000 and $6.09 follow the error.
32. Preferred carrying values (M). Series A $32,800,000, B $58,250,000, C $40,800,000 (total $131,850,000) do not match Charter original issue prices x shares: A 8,200,000 x $1.50 = $12,300,000; B 11,650,000 x $4.25 = $49,512,500; C 6,800,000 x $8.75 = $59,500,000 (total $121,312,500). Series C carrying below its liquidation preference. Preferred described as "redeemable"; only Series C is redeemable (4.6(h), A and B 'not redeemable').
34. Audit/staleness (M). Experts: financials as of 12/31/2023 and 2022 with three years of operations; capitalization at 9/30/2024; Summary says TTM data "derived from audited" statements though TTM is unaudited. Confirm interim-period/age requirements for a 2025 effective date (unverified). Prelim is an excerpt: missing MD&A, Business, Management, Principal Stockholders, executive compensation, related-party sections, which cross-references cite.
35. Consistent items (L). 11,500,000 firm shares (8,500,000/3,000,000), 6.5% discount ($1.235), $19.00 midpoint, 50,850,000 post-offering, Clearfield, Pennington Frost, counsel and tax counsel, ATBM, Durham address. Prelim underwriter allocation table is blank ([●]); UA Schedule II: Stonebridge 7,475,000/Pelham 2,300,000/Lanyard 1,725,000.

D. NEXT STEPS
Obtain and diff the actual IPO Charter, prior charters, stock ledger, investor agreements and consents; cure item 1 first; conform greenshoe, cap table, lock-up, expenses and indemnity across UA/Prelim and rerun dilution; fix UA 3(d)/3(k) timing or re-date UA; obtain Series A/B/C conversion, amendment and debt-covenant consents; add selling stockholder, related-party and indemnification disclosure; confirm settlement cycle. Minor: evergreen base differs; UA 6(f) is not an opinion.

UNVERIFIED: DGCL 204/205 consequences; Rule 15c6-1 cycle; Salzberg holding; financial staleness rule; FINRA expense treatment.
